The atomic bomb. Developed during World War Two by the Manhattan Project from theoretical physics breakthroughs in the nineteen thirties, it derived explosive force from uranium or plutonium fission. First tested successfully in New Mexico on July sixteenth, nineteen forty-five, producing an explosion equivalent to twenty thousand tons of dynamite, it was then dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August, killing over two hundred thousand people. It sparked immediate moral reconsideration, becoming central to Cold War nuclear deterrence strategy based on mutual annihilation.
